author: billmac3
text: Hi Frosty and AK - After a good night's rest (and lots of problem-solving), I've a got new idea on this puzzler. If we apply the 2nd 'promise' of RTM as shown here: the break of FL A to X ALLOWS for a RT to Z. If there's a good approach towards Z, we arePROMISED the next opposing FL above X before a break of B. This works nicely with FOF that states that price will want to go higher than X and also because X engulfed FL A. If price breaks the FL of B then I believe FOF states that price will want to go to the ORFL, which could be either FL C of FL D. I think the other option price has, is to RT from X to somewhere before Z and then engulf X, not going to FLs C or D. I think Staurum threw those in there to misdirect our attention, as a good magician should.

author: Rinehart
text:
Heck, I suppose I don't know the correct answer to that question Frosty because I don't think I've found it on the site explained to my satisfaction. I do however know what I figured out from doing homework, staring at charts, and material I found posted by an old master who is gone.

I know everyone is crazy about LSK because IF has shown us how useful they can be for anticipating monster trades. I haven't fallen in love with them. I am however in love with liquidity gaps (LQGs).

My logic goes like this: * LQGs are poles. Only IT can form poles so I know there should be left over orders at the decision point to create the pole. * If the LQGs is visible on Monthly or Weekly, that is a much stronger indication of IT involvement than a 15 min LQG. * I like to trade HTF because of work. So when I'm planning my trades, I look at the LQGs that match up with my trade area. If I'm trading a zone that has a 4hr LQG, I'm normally looking for a 4hr target.

* If I'm trading a zone that has a Weekly LQG, I'm looking for a Weekly target.

* If I'm trading a zone that has a 4hr, Daily, Weekly, Monthly LQGs all in the same zone. I'm looking for the Monthly target! This is how I was able to get 1200 pips out of the USDCAD short from the beginning of my journal.

Now LQGs just like everything else are a piece of the puzzle for me. But they are very very helpful for me.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Hi all, An FL is created when an important barrier is broken. This so-called important barrier can be any of the following: opposing FL, important SR, PCP, end of CP, and QM level.

When it comes to classifying the scale of an FL, we really only need to use two criteria: 1) It's accomplishment - what time scale does the broken barrier belong to?

2) It's visibility - On what time scale is the FL visible?

Now, I see many people still get confused on the issue of scale. When we call something an H4 FL, what do we mean by that, what is an H4 FL? I have not yet come across a definitely guideline on this. Some people call it an H4 FL because it is visible on H4 time frame, but I have recently ask Master IF about this, and he seemed to imply that it's not about visibility, it's more about its accomplishment: So let's say we have a clear swing high/low on H4 being broken/engulfed by a long extended candle (a pole) on H4 timeframe, so we are not going to see a kink on that long candle, but we will find a kink on 1-min chart that coincide with the swing high/low, so this kink visible only on 1-min chart, is actually a H4 kink. And if you can recall, IF has said it several times that we absolutely must go down to the lowest possible timeframe to find our kink.

However, a subsequent post by Master IF confused me Because he seemed to imply in the above post that visibility is what we should use to classify the scale of an FL.

Hence, the quest for the ultimate truth is still on-going....

cheers AK
